name: J.Press
why: The original campus clothier — the sack suit, the must-iron oxford, and the Shaggy Dog Shetland, sold essentially unchanged since 1902.
origin: Jacobi Press, on the Yale campus, 1902 — owned since 1986 by Japan's Onward Kashiyama, which kept American Ivy alive when America lost interest.
opview: Positions itself as the keeper of authentic American Ivy style — the same clothes, on principle.

notes.ivy: the source code — the same sack suit since 1902, canonized by the 1965 Japanese photo book Take Ivy
notes.finbro: the uniform of the finance bro's grandfather — law professors, old Washington, the bow-tie corner of the firm
notes.prep: The shop the Preppy Handbook actually names, still on the same streets. Where other brands reference the register, this one is a primary source for it.
notes.racquet: New Haven, and the squash-club register is close to native — the shop was built to dress the people who were already members. Little translation required.

cities: New Haven (York St, since 1902) · NYC · Washington DC · more stores in Japan than America

marks: On house goods: NONE. Harris Tweed 7 (licensed protected cloth appellation, not a performance technology)
Shaggy Dog 15 (house garment name, never carries (R))
merino 21 / elastane 2 composition_only. All true technology marks on the site sit on STOCKED third-party labels
